title: Implement tokenizer cost profiling

scope.assurance_scope: PCSM Python v1 tokenizer-cost profiling implementation selection and current-tree capability assessment
scope.implementation_delta: Reuse self_improvement.supervisor_token_ledger as the current-head tokenizer cost-profiling authority. It has explicit versioned provider/model/tokenizer envelopes, content-addressed native and calibrated-fallback token records, exact-once lifecycle reconciliation, and dedicated positive and negative tests. The declared output authority permits no source change; creating a second PCSM profiler, tokenizer, or token ledger would duplicate the existing authority. No actual provider-native observation or calibration is admitted for this PCSM tree, so the receipt records those profile values as unavailable rather than inventing measurements or estimates.

selected_existing_authority.selection: ipfs_accelerate_py.agent_supervisor.self_improvement.supervisor_token_ledger.ProviderModelEnvelope, TokenizerCalibrationSample, FallbackTokenizerCalibration, ProviderTokenUsage, TokenAttribution, and SupervisorTokenLedger
selected_existing_authority.minimum_delta_reason: This is the smallest existing Python-v1 implementation that profiles tokenizer cost without treating a token count as authority: it records measured native usage, permits only envelope-bound replayable fallback estimates, reconciles every lifecycle event exactly once, and keeps failed, rejected, abandoned, retry, reused, speculative, tool, and cancelled tokens explicit without double charging.
selected_existing_authority.version_and_cid_binding: Every selected record inherits CanonicalContract and has a content-derived identity. A ProviderModelEnvelope binds provider_id, model_id, model_revision, tokenizer_id, envelope_revision, and max_context_tokens. A fallback calibration carries a content-derived calibration_id over that exact envelope, calibration revision, and sorted source-free byte/token samples; calibrated use must name that ID. A SupervisorTokenLedger is content-addressed and binds its ResultBinding, complete lifecycle population, terminal attributions, token attributions, and calibration population. Claimed IDs and derived report fields are recomputed and rejected on mismatch.

measurement_and_estimation_contract.measured_provider_native: UsageSource.PROVIDER_NATIVE records supplied input, output, tool, reused, speculative, retry, failed-attempt, cancelled, and cost counters in ProviderTokenUsage. These are usage observations only, not proof, mutation, validation, promotion, or completion authority.
measurement_and_estimation_contract.estimated_calibrated_fallback: UsageSource.CALIBRATED_FALLBACK requires a matching envelope-bound calibration_id. FallbackTokenizerCalibration.estimate_bytes deterministically computes ceil(utf8_bytes * sum(provider_tokens) / sum(utf8_bytes)) from its admitted samples, and exposes maximum_absolute_error_bps over those samples. It is explicitly estimated evidence, never provider-native measured evidence.
measurement_and_estimation_contract.simulated_fixture_boundary: The focused test fixtures construct synthetic envelopes and counters to exercise contract invariants. Their numbers are simulated test data and are not PCSM production measurements or estimates.
measurement_and_estimation_contract.unavailable_current_pcsm_profile: No provider/model/tokenizer envelope, provider-native usage observation, fallback calibration, or sealed PCSM profile ledger bound to this outer tree is present in the admitted current source forest. The current PCSM token cost therefore has no measured or calibrated estimated value in this receipt.

selected_existing_authority.reconciliation_and_authority_boundary: The ledger requires a non-empty complete lifecycle population, exactly one attribution per event, unique measurements and calibrations, matching result bindings, and terminal attribution reconciliation. Its fixed authority bounds are false for authorizes_usage, rewrites_provider_settlement, is_completion_evidence, and is_correctness_evidence. It profiles costs but cannot authorize M2/M3 mutation, proof acceptance, validation acceptance, promotion, or task completion.

current_pcsm_profile.disposition: The profiling implementation is current-head and reusable, but this receipt does not mint a profile instance without an exact envelope and observations. Future consumers must bind a newly emitted ledger to the then-current PCSM tree and reject stale bindings.

evidence_summary.measured: Bound outer and admitted gitlink identities, clean/freshness checks, scheduler and source/test SHA-256 and Git-blob identities, selected explicit @1 schemas and content-identity behavior, source-search result, sealed required pytest result (11 passed), and sealed focused package result (21 passed).
evidence_summary.estimated: The selected implementation has a deterministic calibrated fallback algorithm, but no PCSM-bound calibration or derived token-cost estimate exists at this head; this receipt reports no numeric estimate.
evidence_summary.simulated: Focused-test fixtures use synthetic provider/tokenizer envelopes and counters. They prove the exercised contract checks only and are not production profile evidence.
evidence_summary.unavailable: A PCSM-bound provider/model/tokenizer envelope; provider-native usage; fallback calibration and numeric estimate; a complete PCSM ledger/profile CID; emitted PCSM SourceLinkReceipt/source-map CID; formal-prover result; and a self-describing immutable CID for this receipt.

limitations: The selected ledger is a reusable profiler, not a claim that the current PCSM tree has a measured token cost. A count cannot be manufactured from grammar byte bounds or test fixtures.
Provider-native usage is measured only when supplied by the bound provider envelope; fallback usage remains calibrated estimated evidence and must never be relabeled measured.

The current residual benchmark says no learned tokenizer or model is admitted. Its tokenizer identifiers and the context compiler's generic UTF-8 fallback do not substitute for a bound profile ledger.

Only the declared receipt was changed. A later task that emits an actual profile must create it through the selected existing contract, bind the then-current tree, and add its own receipt rather than mutating this conclusion.
This receipt has no immutable self-CID because minting a self-describing CID would change its bytes.
